sceneFacts.factHeader: Bradley Cooper learned how to 'annihilate' a kitchen.

factBeats.text: To prepare for his character's violent outburst, Bradley Cooper asked chef consultant Marcus Wareing for a demonstration.
Wareing 'absolutely annihilated the whole kitchen' to show Cooper how to portray the intense scene.
The chef drew on his own past experiences to inspire the actor's performance.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Ever wonder about this Burger King?
sceneFacts.factHeader: This Burger King was a real filming location.

factBeats.text: Director John Wells confirmed that the production filmed "right across the street right here at the Burger King" in Leicester Square.
Actor Bradley Cooper reportedly spent a Sunday evening at this Burger King, learning to cook fries and flip burgers as part of his preparation for the film.
Customers at the Burger King were reportedly served by Bradley Cooper during his preparation for the role.
Background extras were cast to sit inside the Burger King, pretending to be customers during filming.

sceneFacts.proactivePrompt: Ever wonder about the real meaning behind this shared meal?
sceneFacts.factHeader: The "family meal" scene was designed as a pivotal moment for Adam's acceptance.

factBeats.text: Culinary advisor Mario Batali stated that Adam sharing a family meal with his staff was intended to be the most "crystallized moment" of him finally joining the team.
Batali explained that the scene aimed to convey the satisfaction of the whole team realizing Adam was truly part of their family.
Actor Bradley Cooper noted he hadn't experienced this tradition in his own restaurant work, underscoring the insider knowledge from the film's culinary consultants.
